questions.title: Homologous chromosome pairing enables genetic recombination
questions.subject: dev
questions.question: Homologous chromosome pairing is a critically important event in meiosis because it is strictly necessary for which process?

explanations.A: Incorrect. General inheritance of traits does not itself require homologous pairing as a mechanism; homologous pairing's specific structural role is to enable the exchange of DNA segments between chromatids.
explanations.B: Correct. During prophase of meiosis I, homologous chromosomes physically pair (synapsis) along their length via the synaptonemal complex, and only while aligned in this way can non-sister chromatids exchange corresponding DNA segments at chiasmata — genetic recombination — producing new combinations of maternal and paternal alleles. Without this length-wise pairing, non-sister chromatids could never align closely enough to exchange DNA segments in the first place.
explanations.C: Incorrect. DNA replication occurs earlier, during the S phase preceding meiosis, and does not require homologous chromosome pairing; pairing is a prophase I event, well after replication is complete.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Targeted DNA repair is a distinct cellular process from meiotic recombination and does not depend on homologous chromosome pairing in the meiotic sense described here.

questions.learning_objective: State that pairing (synapsis) of homologous chromosomes during meiosis I is the structural requirement that permits crossing-over and thus genetic recombination between maternal and paternal chromatids.
